As of 330 AM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Chance for showers and storms today and Tuesday as a 
slow-moving front moves in and lingers across the area.

Early morning surface analysis shows a broad area of high pressure 
set up over Ontario, Canada extending outwards into New England and 
portions of the Mid-Atlantic. A cold front is currently draped 
across the northern VA border as of this writing and is progged to 
slowly push southward across our area through the day today. It will 
likely take most of the day to reach NC, which will impact both
our temperature and precipitation forecast for today. First of 
all, let's note that winds will become NNE as the front passes 
through. Additionally, low cloud cover will also develop along 
and behind the front, and will likely linger into tomorrow. 
There could also be some patchy ground fog this morning ahead of
the front. The front will create quite a temperature gradient 
across the CWA today, with highs topping out in the upper 70s to
around 80 degrees for ~Ashland and north. To the south, highs 
will be able to jump into the upper 80s. Our furthest south 
points in NE NC will likely hit 90 degrees today. 

The precipitation forecast is a bit tricky today due to the timing 
and placement of the front, but the better chances for showers and 
storms will be along and south of the front where some somewhat 
decent instability will exist - so roughly US-460 and south. SPC has 
a Marginal Risk of severe weather along and west of I-95, with the 
main threat still being damaging winds. Hi-res guidance has trended 
the timing of any storms a bit later to late this evening, 
especially closer to the VA/NC border. Models are then in decent 
agreement of rain chances becoming more widespread overnight. Lows 
tonight will be in the mid to upper 60s for most everyone. On 
Tuesday, the Canadian high pressure shifts a bit eastward, serving 
as a reinforcement of our onshore flow. Northeast winds will begin 
to pick up along the Eastern Shore Tuesday morning, then spreading 
to all coastal locations through the day. Widespread (coastal)
gusts to 25mph will be likely, with gusts increasing to 
35-45mph along the Atlantic coast of the Eastern Shore 
(including Ocean City, Chincoteague, etc) Tuesday night into 
Wednesday. The lingering front will keep rain chances going on 
Tuesday for most of the area. Could get some isolated storms as 
well that create locally heavy downpours and instances of flash 
flooding. The cooler airmass will make its presence known 
starting Tuesday night as lows will be in the upper 50s across 
the northwest, with low to mid 60s inland and upper 60s along 
the SE and coastal areas. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Persistent onshore flow and a strengthening coastal 
low will create a wetter, cooler, and breezier forecast for most of 
the week.

Cold air damming will overtake the area on Wednesday as high 
pressure remains parked to our north. This will keep high 
temperatures in the low to mid 60s for the northern and western
inland areas, with low to mid 70s for the SE half of the CWA. 
Winds for coastal areas will persistently be blowing around 
20-25mph with gusts to 35+mph. The strongest winds will once 
again be along the Atlantic coast of the Eastern Shore with 
gusts to 40-45mph likely Tuesday night, potentially lasting all 
the way through Friday/Saturday as the low pressure remains 
offshore. Rain chances continue everywhere on Wednesday, though 
due to the stable cooler environment, storms aren't expected, 
with the exception of the NC coast. There could once again be 
areas of locally higher rainfall at times that lead to flash 
flooding. WPC has a Marginal Risk of Excessive Rainfall for a 
majority of the area on Wednesday. Rain chances may focus more 
across the eastern portions of the area later Thursday into 
Friday. A secondary surface low may form and cause the main low 
to recenter itself slightly closer to the Mid-Atlantic/New 
England coast late Thursday into Friday. Highs will remain in 
the mid to upper 60s with 70s closer to the coast both day. If 
winds are able to shift more out of the north around the west 
side of the low pressure, our low temperatures Thursday and 
Friday night could dip into the mid 50s, with the potential for 
lower 50s inland. 

Into the weekend and beyond, models are showing that this low may 
continue to hang around to our northeast. As of right now, it 
may be just far enough from our area that we could get a break 
in the rainy conditions for the weekend, but that definitely 
could change as the details of the low's placement come to 
light. The 00Z GFS run even has the stubborn coastal low 
meandering back down south to the VA/NC line to start the new 
work week. Be sure to stay tuned to the latest forecast updates 
as this system will create a prolonged period of gusty onshore 
winds, coastal flooding, high surf, beach erosion, and dangerous
marine conditions (see below).
